name: Pregabalin
summary: A gabapentinoid with linear absorption and predictable kinetics, used for neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, and adjunctive seizure control.
mechanism: Binds the α2δ subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, reducing calcium influx and the release of excitatory neurotransmitters such as glutamate.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Days to 2 weeks for neuropathic pain effect
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Minimal; largely renal excretion of unchanged drug

dosing.adult: Start 50–75 mg BID; usual maintenance 150–300 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses
dosing.renalAdjustment: Required — reduce dose in renal impairment (CrCl <60 mL/min)

safety.pregnancy: Limited human data; animal studies showed fetal harm — avoid unless clearly needed
warnings: Dizziness and somnolence — impair driving and machinery operation
Abrupt withdrawal can precipitate seizures — taper over at least 1 week
Peripheral edema and weight gain are common and can be dose-limiting
Misuse/abuse potential (Schedule V in the US)
Class warning: suicidal thoughts and behavior
safety.overdose: Drowsiness, confusion, agitation; supportive care; hemodialysis is effective

indications: Neuropathic pain (diabetic peripheral neuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia)
Generalized anxiety disorder (approved in some regions)
clinicalPearls: Linear absorption gives predictable exposure and faster titration than gabapentin
Still taper on withdrawal — abrupt stop can trigger seizures even at standard doses
good: Neuropathic pain or fibromyalgia needing faster onset and BID dosing.
bad: Patients bothered by edema/weight gain, or whose work or driving is impaired by sedation.
